video.title: 磷的发现
video.title_en: The Man Who Put the Pee in Phosphorus

summary.text: 1669年，德国炼金术士亨尼格·布兰德（Hennig Brand）在汉堡的地下室里进行了一次疯狂的实验。为了寻找传说中能将贱金属点化为黄金的“贤者之石”（Philosopher's Stone），他收集了数千升人尿并将其煮沸浓缩。虽然他没能找到金子，但他意外得到了一种白色的、蜡状的物质。这种物质在黑暗中会发出幽灵般的绿光，并且极易燃烧。布兰德将其命名为“Phosphorus”（磷），源自希腊语，意为“光之携带者”。这是人类历史上第一个被有记录地发现的化学元素，它的发现标志着化学从神秘的炼金术向元素发现时代迈出的重要一步。
summary.text_en: In 1669, German alchemist Hennig Brand conducted a mad experiment in his Hamburg basement. In search of the legendary 'Philosopher's Stone' that could turn base metals into gold, he collected thousands of liters of human urine and boiled it down. Although he failed to find gold, he accidentally obtained a white, waxy substance. This substance glowed with a ghostly green light in the dark and was highly flammable. Brand named it 'Phosphorus', from Greek meaning 'Light-Bearer'. This was the first chemical element to be discovered in recorded history, marking a significant step from mystical alchemy to the age of element discovery.
key_points: 历史上第一个被记录发现过程的元素
源于炼金术对“贤者之石”的追求
从数千升人尿中提炼而出
名字 Phosphorus 意为“光之携带者”
开启了化学元素发现的新纪元
key_points_en: First element with a recorded discovery history
Resulted from the alchemical quest for the Philosopher's Stone
Extracted from thousands of liters of human urine
Opened a new era of chemical element discovery

story.text: 布兰德是一个破产的商人，为了致富转行做了炼金术士。他坚信人体是一个小宇宙，而金黄色的尿液中一定含有某种“黄金精华”。为了验证这个疯狂的想法，他设法（据说是从德国军营）收集了约1500加仑（5000多升）的尿液。他把这些尿液放在地下室里腐烂，然后煮沸浓缩成糊状，再通过高温蒸馏。当最后的蒸馏液冷却后，并没有出现黄金，而是凝结成了一种白色的固体。当布兰德关上灯，他被眼前的景象惊呆了：烧瓶里的物质在黑暗中闪烁着神秘的绿光，仿佛把月光封存了起来。他以为自己终于找到了贤者之石，并试图保守这个秘密长达六年，但“夜光物”的消息最终还是震惊了整个欧洲科学界。
story.text_en: Brand was a bankrupt merchant who turned to alchemy to get rich. He believed the human body was a microcosm and that golden urine must contain some 'golden essence'. To test this crazy idea, he managed to collect (reportedly from German army barracks) about 1,500 gallons (over 5,000 liters) of urine. He let it rot in his basement, boiled it into a paste, and then distilled it at high heat. When the final distillate cooled, no gold appeared; instead, it solidified into a white substance. When Brand turned off the lights, he was stunned: the substance in the flask glowed with a mysterious green light, as if he had bottled moonlight. He thought he had found the Philosopher's Stone and tried to keep it secret for six years, but news of the 'noctiluca' eventually shocked the entire European scientific community.

fun_facts.text: 布兰德使用的尿液配方非常重口味：先让尿液放置腐烂直到生出蠕虫，然后再煮沸。他的邻居们一定度过了一段极其难熬的时光。
fun_facts.text_en: Brand's urine recipe was intense: let the urine stand until it putrefies and breeds worms, then boil it. His neighbors must have had a terrible time.

fun_facts.text: 1771年，画家约瑟夫·怀特创作了名画《寻找贤者之石的炼金术士》。画中布兰德跪在发光的烧瓶前祈祷，这幅画完美捕捉了科学发现那一刻的神性与敬畏。
fun_facts.text_en: In 1771, Joseph Wright painted 'The Alchemist in Search of the Philosopher's Stone'. It depicts Brand kneeling in prayer before the glowing flask, capturing the divinity and awe of the moment of scientific discovery.

fun_facts.text: 布兰德发现的是“白磷”，它在空气中会自燃。因为不知道这一点，他在处理这种物质时经常烧伤自己。
fun_facts.text_en: Brand discovered 'white phosphorus', which spontaneously ignites in air. Not knowing this, he frequently burned himself while handling the substance.

simple_explanation.text:
这就好比你为了从沙子里淘金子，煮了整整一游泳池的脏水，结果金子没找到，却意外煮出了一块会发光的宝石。
布兰德就是这么干的。他以为尿液是黄色的所以里面有金子，结果煮出了磷。磷是一种非常活泼的元素，在空气中会慢慢氧化并释放能量，这就是它为什么会发光（磷光）的原因。虽然初衷是迷信的炼金术，但结果却是实实在在的科学发现。
simple_explanation.text_en:
It's like boiling a whole swimming pool of dirty water to find gold in the sand. You don't find gold, but you accidentally boil out a glowing gem.
That's what Brand did. He thought urine had gold because it was yellow, but he got phosphorus instead. Phosphorus is a very reactive element that slowly oxidizes in air and releases energy, which is why it glows (phosphorescence). Although the intent was superstitious alchemy, the result was a solid scientific discovery.

applications.title: 现代农业
applications.text: 磷是植物生长必不可少的元素。今天，全球开采的磷矿石绝大部分都用于制造磷肥，养活了地球上的人口。
applications.text_en: Phosphorus is essential for plant growth. Today, the vast majority of mined phosphate rock is used to make fertilizers, feeding the world's population.

applications.title: 火柴
applications.text: 早期火柴使用有毒的白磷（导致了可怕的‘磷毒颌坏死’病），后来被安全的红磷取代。那是我们随时能取火的开端。
applications.text_en: Early matches used toxic white phosphorus (causing the terrible 'phossy jaw'), which was later replaced by safe red phosphorus. That was the beginning of fire on demand.

applications.title: 生物骨架
applications.text: 磷酸钙是我们骨骼和牙齿的主要成分，也是DNA骨架的关键组成部分。没有磷，就没有生命。
applications.text_en: Calcium phosphate is the main component of our bones and teeth, and a key part of the DNA backbone. Without phosphorus, there is no life.

impact.text: 布兰德的发现具有划时代的意义。它是第一个在有记载的历史中被“个人”发现的元素（古代已知的金银铜铁等都是自古就有的）。这件事向世界证明，除了传统的七种金属外，自然界中还隐藏着未知的基本物质等待被挖掘。它极大地刺激了后来的化学家（如波义耳）去探索物质的本质，从炼金术的迷雾中开辟出了化学的道路。
impact.text_en: Brand's discovery was epoch-making. It was the first element discovered by an 'individual' in recorded history (gold, silver, iron, etc., were known since antiquity). It proved to the world that beyond the traditional seven metals, nature hid unknown fundamental substances waiting to be unearthed. It greatly stimulated later chemists (like Boyle) to explore the nature of matter, blazing a trail for chemistry out of the fog of alchemy.

influenced_by.contribution: 帕拉塞尔苏斯（其理论让炼金术士相信人体分泌物中含有某种神秘的生命精华）
influenced_by.contribution_en: Paracelsus (His theories led alchemists to believe that bodily secretions contained some mystical life essence)

influenced.contribution: 罗伯特·波义耳（在从助手那里得知制法后，改进了提炼过程并系统研究了磷的化学性质）
influenced.contribution_en: Robert Boyle (After learning the recipe from an assistant, he improved the process and systematically studied the chemical properties of phosphorus)

influenced.contribution: 拉瓦锡（最终确认磷不是一种化合物，而是一种不可分解的元素，并将其列入元素表）
influenced.contribution_en: Lavoisier (Finally confirmed that phosphorus was not a compound but an undecomposable element, listing it in his table of elements)

influence_chain.legacy_text: 他为了寻找虚幻的魔法石，却为人类点亮了真实的化学之光。
influence_chain.legacy_text_en: In search of an illusory magic stone, he lit the real lamp of chemistry for humanity.

quiz.question: 亨尼格·布兰德最初收集大量尿液是为了寻找什么？
quiz.question_en: What was Hennig Brand originally looking for when he collected vast amounts of urine?
options: 传说中的贤者之石 (点金石)
quiz.explanation: 作为一名炼金术士，布兰德相信通过浓缩金黄色的尿液可以提炼出能将贱金属转化为黄金的贤者之石。
quiz.explanation_en: As an alchemist, Brand believed that by concentrating golden urine, he could extract the Philosopher's Stone capable of transmuting base metals into gold.
